root_cause.text: In `net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c`, the partial-overlap check in `__nft_rbtree_insert()` incorrectly exempted anonymous sets from validating consecutive start elements, so overlapping intervals like `A-B` and `A-C` could be inserted because the code failed to detect that a new start element was placed before an existing end element.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the overlap logic from unconditionally skipping anonymous-set start/start checks (`if (!nft_set_is_anonymous(set) && rbe_le && nft_rbtree_interval_start(rbe_le) && nft_rbtree_interval_start(new)) return -ENOTEMPTY;`) to also examine the previous active element for anonymous sets (`rbe_prev = nft_rbtree_prev_active(rbe_le); if (rbe_prev && nft_rbtree_interval_end(rbe_prev)) return -ENOTEMPTY;`), and the commit message explicitly says the bug allowed “two start elements with the same, eg. A-B, A-C where C < B.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add previous-element lookup support for anonymous nftables rbtree sets to correct insertion handling when all elements are always active.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function named `nft_rbtree_prev_active()` was added. It takes a `struct nft_rbtree_elem *`, calls `rb_prev(&rbe->node)` to get the previous red-black tree node, returns `NULL` if there is no previous node, and otherwise converts that node back to `struct nft_rbtree_elem *`. In `__nft_rbtree_insert()`, the local variable declaration was expanded to include an additional `struct nft_rbtree_elem *rbe_prev`.
intent_record.how: This change provides a way to locate the immediately preceding tree element for anonymous sets that do not support updates, where all elements are considered active. That enables insertion logic to inspect the previous element when determining placement or adjacency, which can affect how set elements are ordered or linked during insertion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten nftables interval insertion validation to reject partial overlaps in anonymous sets when a new start element falls between an existing start and end element.
intent_record.what: The overlap check for inserting a new interval start element was rewritten. Previously, the code returned -ENOTEMPTY only when the set was not anonymous and both the nearest less-or-equal existing element and the new element were interval starts. Now it first checks that condition, returns -ENOTEMPTY immediately for non-anonymous sets, and for anonymous sets it additionally looks up the previous active element and returns -ENOTEMPTY if that previous element is an interval end.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes insertion validation so anonymous sets no longer blindly allow consecutive start elements. It now detects the case where a new start element would be placed between an existing start and end element, preventing a partial-overlap interval from being inserted and correctly rejecting it with -ENOTEMPTY.
